intro: You are at Amastris, an ancient city in Bartın province, founded in the 4th century BC. It is a harbour city on a peninsula between two bays, and its walls are still in daily use.
history: The city was founded by the Persian princess Amastris. It remained an important port through Roman and Byzantine times, and later the Genoese refortified it.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Kuşkayası Road Monument, the Roman walls, the Bedesten and the Harbour.
facts: Did you know? Queen Amastris founded the city and gave it her own name, making it one of the few ancient cities named for a woman. The Kuşkayası rock relief works as a maintenance record of the Roman road network. Pliny wrote to Trajan asking leave to cover the open sewer running through the city — and the emperor's reply survives too. And the Roman 'Bird Gate' still stands within the street fabric of modern Amasra.
outro: This brings our tour of Amastris to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls are still part of daily life; let them stay that way for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
